desc:
The alphabet consists of the first k lowercase letters (a, b, ... ). The string s uses only letters of this alphabet.

Consider every string over this alphabet. Return the length of the shortest one that is not a subsequence of s.

For example, with k = 3 and s = "abcab" the answer is 2: every single letter occurs in s, but "cc" does not. With k = 2 and s = "abab" the answer is 3, because all four strings of length 2 are subsequences, while "aaa" is not.
constraints: s uses only the first k lowercase letters (it does not have to use all of them)
hints: A string of length L is a non-subsequence if you cannot find it in order. Can you tell how long a string can be that is guaranteed to be found, whatever its letters are?
Cut s from the left into blocks: each block ends as soon as it contains all k letters. Any single letter can be found inside one block.
If you can cut out m such complete blocks, every string of length m is a subsequence (pick letter i from block i). The leftover tail misses some letter, so a string of length m + 1 is not.
editorial: Scan s from the left and keep the set of letters seen in the current block. As soon as the set has all k letters, close the block, increase a counter m and clear the set. The greedy cut gives the largest possible number of blocks.

Every string of length m is a subsequence: take its i-th letter from the i-th block, which contains every letter. On the other hand, the leftover tail after the last block lacks some letter x. Take the string whose first m letters are the letters that closed the blocks, followed by x. Greedy matching of its first m letters ends exactly at the end of the last block, and the tail has no x, so this string of length m + 1 is not a subsequence. Hence the answer is m + 1. Time O(n), space O(k).
